title: OneDrive and SharePoint: annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs in the web viewer
summary: The roadmap facts and existing PowerShell controls are supported. Hold because the governance prose casts doubt on whether label encryption permissions govern the protected content, although Microsoft's documentation explicitly gives them that reach; the narrower question is which rights annotation requires.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Learn documents annotation and markup tools for PDFs in OneDrive generally.
claims.quote: Annotation and markup tools | Easily collaborate and share feedback by using digital ink, highlighting text, drawing shapes, and inserting sticky notes directly onto your PDF files.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Learn documents tenant-enabled processing of sensitivity-label encrypted PDFs in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Enabling this feature also results in SharePoint and OneDrive being able to process the contents of Office files and optionally, PDF documents that have been encrypted by using a sensitivity label.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The PDF support setting is reached through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote:
Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies
Then, if you see a message Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling, select this banner
claims.fix: Append ' > Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling' to controls[0].ui.path and the rendered path. Retain the note that the banner is conditional. The cited page documents selecting that banner to turn on PDF protection.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF $true enables the existing tenant PDF sensitivity-label support.
claims.quote:
-EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF
Allows tenant admins to turn on support for PDFs with sensitivity labels for the following scenarios:
True - Enables support for PDFs.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Running Set-SPOTenant requires a SharePoint Online administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The existing EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF setting defaults to False.
claims.quote: False (default) - Disables support for PDFs.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo requires connecting to each geo-location and running the PDF support command separately.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo: Similarly to the instructions to run the PowerShell command to enable support for sensitivity labels, you must connect to each of your geo-locations, and then run the command to enable support for PDFs.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not state whether annotation specifically depends on EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive SharePoint sensitivity label protected PDF annotation web viewer usage rights default prerequisites EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF. Read PDF support and Set-SPOTenant reference: their scenario lists do not name annotation.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Sensitivity labels page in Microsoft Purview is the starting place for editing a label's Access control permissions.
claims.quote:
Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels
To edit an existing label, select it, and then select the Edit label icon.
claims.fix: The path stops at the correct labels list. Extend it to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Files & other data assets > Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected > Control access > Access control > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now'. The last steps are documented at the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels; retain that source.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-Label with Identity and EncryptionRightsDefinitions modifies the specified label's user rights.
claims.quote: The EncryptionRightsDefinitions parameter specifies the rights users have when accessing protected. This parameter uses the syntax Identity1:Rights1,Rights2;Identity2:Rights3,Rights4.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-Label runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[1].governs; Governance controls
claims.claim: A label's assigned encryption permissions determine users' rights to the content that label encrypts, rather than being a setting for one annotated file.
claims.quote: Assign permissions now, so that you determine exactly which users get which permissions to content with that label.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The correctly documented label encryption control is accompanied by the caveat 'Not stated to govern annotation.'
claims.quote:
When a document, email, or meeting invite is encrypted, access to the content is restricted, so that it:
Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.
claims.fix: Replace 'Not stated to govern annotation.' with 'The label encryption settings restrict access to the content; the rights required specifically for annotation are not yet documented.' Keep the existing Access control and PowerShell notes.

claims.where: Governance controls: paragraph after table
claims.claim: Learn does not say that either existing control governs the annotation feature itself, so both should be treated only as preparation.
claims.quote: When users download or access these files from SharePoint or OneDrive, the sensitivity label and any encryption settings from the label are enforced and remain with the file, wherever it's stored.
claims.fix: Replace 'Learn does not say that either governs the annotation feature itself, so treat them as ways to prepare the tenant rather than as a switch for it.' with 'Label encryption settings govern access to the protected content. Which usage rights annotation requires, and whether it depends on the PDF support setting in row 1, are not yet documented.' The cited SharePoint/OneDrive page and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels establish this general reach without specifying the annotation rights.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Edit Content, Edit is a usage right distinct from Save.
claims.quote: Common name: Edit Content, Edit Encoding in policy: DOCEDIT | Allows the user to modify, rearrange, format, or sort the content inside the application, which includes Office on the web. It doesn't grant the right to save the edited copy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Save is a separately defined usage right.
claims.quote: Common name: Save Encoding in policy: EDIT | Allows the user to save the item to the current location. In Office on the web, it also allows the user to edit the content.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The usage rights or combination of rights specifically required by this planned annotation capability are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive protected PDFs annotation usage rights. Read usage-rights reference, OneDrive PDF features, SharePoint/OneDrive label support and roadmap. COMMENT is defined generally, but no source identifies the rights this planned web annotation capability requires.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: On-premises-key encryption does not gain normal service content processing from enabling label support.
claims.quote: If encryption has been applied with an on-premises key ... the service behavior for processing the file contents doesn't change. So for these files, coauthoring, eDiscovery, data loss prevention, search, and other collaborative features won't work.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Double Key Encryption does not gain normal service content processing from enabling label support.
claims.quote:
SharePoint and OneDrive can't process encrypted files when the label that applied the encryption has either of the following configurations for encryption:
User access to content expires is set to a value other than Never.
Double Key Encryption is selected.

claims.quote: users who have the appropriate usage rights can annotate these protected PDFs in place in their browser while preserving the file's sensitivity label, encryption, and usage rights when changes are saved.
